blocks.explanation:
Humein dikhana hai ke jis angle ka cosine \(\frac{8}{17}\) hai, usi angle ka sine \(\frac{15}{17}\) hai; yani dono taraf ek hi angle ke do naam hain.
Tareeqa wohi jo Example 6 mein hai: left side ko \(\alpha\) ka naam do, \(\sin^2\alpha + \cos^2\alpha = 1\) se \(\sin\alpha\) nikalo, quadrant se sign faisla karo.
Aakhir mein yeh zaroor check karo ke \(\alpha\) \(\sin^{-1}\) ki principal range mein hai, warna \(\alpha = \sin^{-1}(\sin\alpha)\) likhna ghalat hoga.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\cos^{-1}\frac{8}{17}\).
Saabit karna: \(\cos^{-1}\frac{8}{17} = \sin^{-1}\frac{15}{17}\).
Tareeqa: \(\cos^{-1}\frac{8}{17} = \alpha\) maan lenge. \(\sin\alpha\) nikalenge; agar \(\alpha\) range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein ho to \(\alpha = \sin^{-1}(\sin\alpha)\) likh sakte hain.

Angle ko naam dein
\[\cos^{-1}\frac{8}{17} = \alpha \Rightarrow \cos\alpha = \frac{8}{17}\]
\[\alpha \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\]
Kyun: \(\cos^{-1}\) ka jawab hamesha \([0, \pi]\) mein hota hai. Yahan \(\cos\alpha\) positive hai, aur \([0, \pi]\) mein cosine sirf pehle quadrant mein positive hota hai. Is liye \(\alpha\) pehle quadrant mein hai.

\(\sin\alpha\) nikalein
\[\sin\alpha = \pm\sqrt{1 - \cos^2\alpha}\]
\[= \pm\sqrt{1 - \frac{64}{289}} = \pm\sqrt{\frac{225}{289}}\]
\[= \pm\frac{15}{17}\]
Kyun: Basic identity \(\sin^2\alpha + \cos^2\alpha = 1\) se \(\sin^2\alpha = 1 - \cos^2\alpha\). \(1 - \frac{64}{289} = \frac{289 - 64}{289} = \frac{225}{289}\), aur \(\sqrt{225} = 15\), \(\sqrt{289} = 17\).

Sign chunein
\[\sin\alpha = \frac{15}{17}\]
Kyun: Square root se \(\pm\) aata hai, lekin \(\alpha\) pehle quadrant mein hai jahan sine positive hai, is liye plus wala sign rakha.
Dhyan dein: Sign ka faisla quadrant se hota hai, andaze se nahi. Yahi qadam proof ki jaan hai.

Wapas inverse mein badlein
\[\alpha = \sin^{-1}\frac{15}{17}\]
\[\cos^{-1}\frac{8}{17} = \sin^{-1}\frac{15}{17}\]
Kyun: \(\alpha\) ka interval \(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) poora \(\sin^{-1}\) ki range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) ke andar hai. Is liye \(\sin\alpha = \frac{15}{17}\) se seedha \(\alpha = \sin^{-1}\frac{15}{17}\) likh sakte hain. Phir \(\alpha\) ki jagah us ki asal value rakh di.

Tasdeeq
\[8^2 + 15^2 = 64 + 225 = 289 = 17^2\]
Kyun: 8, 15, 17 ek right triangle ki sides hain (Pythagoras). Jis angle ki adjacent side 8 aur hypotenuse 17 hai, us ki opposite side 15 hai; is liye us ka sine \(\frac{15}{17}\) hai. Dono tareeqon se ek hi natija.

blocks.explanation:
Left side ko \(\alpha\) ka naam denge. Phir \(\csc\alpha = \frac{5}{4}\) hoga, aur reciprocal se \(\sin\alpha = \frac{4}{5}\).
\(\sin^2\alpha + \cos^2\alpha = 1\) se \(\cos\alpha\) nikalenge aur quadrant se sign faisla karenge.
Aakhir mein check karenge ke \(\alpha\) \(\cos^{-1}\) ki range \([0, \pi]\) mein hai, taake \(\alpha = \cos^{-1}(\cos\alpha)\) likh sakein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\csc^{-1}\frac{5}{4}\).
Saabit karna: \(\csc^{-1}\frac{5}{4} = \cos^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\).
Tareeqa: \(\csc^{-1}\frac{5}{4} = \alpha\) maan kar pehle \(\sin\alpha\), phir \(\cos\alpha\) nikalenge, aur range check kar ke wapas \(\cos^{-1}\) mein likhenge.

Angle ko naam dein
\[\csc^{-1}\frac{5}{4} = \alpha \Rightarrow \csc\alpha = \frac{5}{4}\]
\[\sin\alpha = \frac{4}{5}, \quad \alpha \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\]
Kyun: Cosecant ka reciprocal sine hai, is liye \(\frac{5}{4}\) palat kar \(\frac{4}{5}\) bana. \(\csc^{-1}\) ki range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) hai; value positive hai to \(\alpha\) positive hissa \(\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hai.

\(\cos\alpha\) nikalein
\[\cos\alpha = \pm\sqrt{1 - \sin^2\alpha}\]
\[= \pm\sqrt{1 - \frac{16}{25}} = \pm\frac{3}{5}\]
\[\cos\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\]
Kyun: \(1 - \frac{16}{25} = \frac{9}{25}\) aur \(\sqrt{\frac{9}{25}} = \frac{3}{5}\). Pehle quadrant mein cosine positive hota hai, is liye plus sign rakha.
Dhyan dein: \(\csc\alpha = \frac{5}{4}\) ko seedha \(\cos\alpha\) ka reciprocal samajh lena aam ghalti hai; cosecant sine ka reciprocal hai, cosine ka nahi.

Wapas inverse mein badlein
\[\alpha = \cos^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\]
\[\csc^{-1}\frac{5}{4} = \cos^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\]
Kyun: \(\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) poora \(\cos^{-1}\) ki range \([0, \pi]\) ke andar hai. Is liye \(\cos\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\) se \(\alpha = \cos^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\) seedha likh sakte hain.

Tasdeeq
\[3^2 + 4^2 = 5^2\]
Kyun: 3-4-5 wala mashhoor right triangle. Jis angle ke saamne 4 hai, us ka \(\csc = \frac{5}{4}\) (hypotenuse/opposite) aur \(\cos = \frac{3}{5}\) (adjacent/hypotenuse). Dono taraf ek hi angle.

blocks.explanation:
\(\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4}\) ko \(\alpha\) kahein to left side \(2\alpha\) ban jata hai, yani asal mein double angle ka sawal hai.
Double-angle formula \(\tan 2\alpha = \frac{2\tan\alpha}{1 - \tan^2\alpha}\) se \(\tan 2\alpha\) nikalenge.
Phir zaroori check: kya \(2\alpha\) bhi \(\tan^{-1}\) ki range \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) mein hai? Agar haan, to \(2\alpha = \tan^{-1}(\tan 2\alpha)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(2\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4}\).
Saabit karna: \(2\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4} = \tan^{-1}\frac{24}{7}\).
Tareeqa: \(\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4} = \alpha\) maan kar double-angle formula se \(\tan 2\alpha\) nikalenge, phir range check kar ke wapas \(\tan^{-1}\) mein likhenge.

Angle ko naam dein
\[\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4} = \alpha \Rightarrow \tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}\]
\[0 < \alpha < \frac{\pi}{4}\]
Kyun: \(\tan\alpha\) positive hai, to \(\alpha\) range ke positive hisse \(\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) mein hai. Aur \(\frac{3}{4}\) chhota hai \(1 = \tan\frac{\pi}{4}\) se; tangent barhta hua (increasing) function hai, is liye \(\alpha < \frac{\pi}{4}\). Yeh baat aage kaam aayegi.

Double-angle formula
\[\tan 2\alpha = \frac{2\tan\alpha}{1 - \tan^2\alpha}\]
\[= \dfrac{2 \cdot \frac{3}{4}}{1 - \frac{9}{16}} = \dfrac{\frac{3}{2}}{\frac{7}{16}}\]
\[= \frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{16}{7} = \frac{24}{7}\]
Kyun: Yeh formula \(\tan(\alpha + \beta)\) mein \(\beta = \alpha\) rakhne se aata hai. Upar \(2 \cdot \frac{3}{4} = \frac{3}{2}\), neeche \(1 - \frac{9}{16} = \frac{7}{16}\). Fraction ko fraction se divide karne ke liye neeche wale ko ulta kar ke multiply kiya: \(\frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{16}{7} = \frac{48}{14} = \frac{24}{7}\).
Dhyan dein: \(\tan^2\alpha = \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{16}\) hai, \(\frac{3}{16}\) nahi; upar aur neeche dono ka square hota hai.

Wapas inverse mein badlein
\[0 < 2\alpha < \frac{\pi}{2}\]
\[2\alpha = \tan^{-1}\frac{24}{7}\]
\[2\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4} = \tan^{-1}\frac{24}{7}\]
Kyun: \(\alpha < \frac{\pi}{4}\) tha, to \(2\alpha < \frac{\pi}{2}\). Yani \(2\alpha\) bhi \(\tan^{-1}\) ki range mein hai, is liye \(\tan 2\alpha = \frac{24}{7}\) se \(2\alpha = \tan^{-1}\frac{24}{7}\) likhna jaiz hai. Agar \(2\alpha\) range se bahar hota to yeh qadam ghalat hota.

Tasdeeq
\[\tan^{-1}0.75 \approx 0.6435\]
\[2(0.6435) = 1.2870 \approx \tan^{-1}\frac{24}{7}\]
Kyun: Calculator (radian mode) se dekha: \(\tan^{-1}\frac{24}{7} = \tan^{-1}3.4286 \approx 1.2870\). Dono barabar hain.

blocks.explanation:
\(\sin^{-1}\frac{7}{25}\) ko \(\alpha\) kahein to left side \(2\alpha\) hai; phir double angle ka formula lagega.
\(\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\) mein \(\cos\alpha\) bhi chahiye, jo identity \(\sin^2\alpha + \cos^2\alpha = 1\) se milega.
Aakhir mein check karenge ke \(2\alpha\) \(\sin^{-1}\) ki range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hai; yahi proof ka sab se nazuk hissa hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(2\sin^{-1}\frac{7}{25}\).
Saabit karna: \(2\sin^{-1}\frac{7}{25} = \sin^{-1}\frac{336}{625}\).
Tareeqa: \(\sin^{-1}\frac{7}{25} = \alpha\) maan kar \(\cos\alpha\) nikalenge, phir \(\sin 2\alpha\), phir range check kar ke wapas \(\sin^{-1}\) mein likhenge.

Angle ko naam dein
\[\sin^{-1}\frac{7}{25} = \alpha \Rightarrow \sin\alpha = \frac{7}{25}\]
\[\alpha \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\]
Kyun: \(\sin^{-1}\) ka jawab \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hota hai, aur sine positive hai to \(\alpha\) positive hisse mein hai.

\(\cos\alpha\) nikalein
\[\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - \frac{49}{625}} = \sqrt{\frac{576}{625}}\]
\[= \frac{24}{25}\]
Kyun: \(1 - \frac{49}{625} = \frac{576}{625}\), aur \(\sqrt{576} = 24\), \(\sqrt{625} = 25\). Pehle quadrant mein cosine positive, is liye sirf plus sign.

Double-angle formula
\[\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\]
\[= 2 \cdot \frac{7}{25} \cdot \frac{24}{25} = \frac{336}{625}\]
Kyun: \(\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\) wala formula. Upar \(2 \times 7 \times 24 = 336\), neeche \(25 \times 25 = 625\).
Dhyan dein: \(\sin 2\alpha\) ko \(2\sin\alpha\) samajh lena (yani \(\frac{14}{25}\)) sab se aam ghalti hai; double angle ka sine do guna nahi hota.

Kya \(2\alpha\) range mein hai?
\[\sin\alpha = \frac{7}{25} = 0.28 < \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[0 < \alpha < \frac{\pi}{4} \Rightarrow 0 < 2\alpha < \frac{\pi}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\sin\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707\). \(0.28\) us se chhota hai, aur pehle quadrant mein sine barhta hai, is liye \(\alpha < \frac{\pi}{4}\). Double karne par bhi \(2\alpha < \frac{\pi}{2}\), yani range ke andar.

Wapas inverse mein badlein
\[2\alpha = \sin^{-1}\frac{336}{625}\]
\[2\sin^{-1}\frac{7}{25} = \sin^{-1}\frac{336}{625}\]
Kyun: \(2\alpha\) range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hai, is liye \(\sin 2\alpha = \frac{336}{625}\) se \(2\alpha = \sin^{-1}\frac{336}{625}\) likhna sahi hai.

Tasdeeq
\[2\sin^{-1}0.28 \approx 2(0.2838) = 0.5676\]
\[\sin^{-1}0.5376 \approx 0.5676\]
Kyun: Calculator (radian mode) se dono taraf barabar aaye. \(\frac{336}{625} = 0.5376\).
